title: Prepay, contest or appeal a traffic ticket
question: Can I pay my Charlottesville traffic ticket without going to court?
office: Charlottesville General District Court, Clerk's Office (Traffic Division)
summary: Yes, for most tickets. If the offence is on the Supreme Court's Uniform Fine Schedule, you can prepay the Charlottesville General District Court online (4% card fee, by 3:30 pm the business day before trial), by mail (it must arrive before the court date) or at the Clerk's Office, 606 E Market Street. Prepaying is a guilty plea, and the conviction goes to DMV. The court adds $74 in costs to an infraction fine. Reckless driving (including speeding 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph), DUI, driving while suspended or unlicensed, and leaving the scene cannot be prepaid. To contest, go to trial on the summons date; a judge decides a traffic infraction without a jury. After a conviction the court must offer a payment plan, and you can appeal to the Circuit Court within 10 days, where you can have a jury.

steps.step: Find out which court has the ticket and what it charges
steps.who: Person charged (the driver named on the summons)
steps.how: The summons names the court at the top; pay or appear in that court. A ticket for an offence in the city is normally returnable to the Charlottesville General District Court, and a ticket written elsewhere (for example in Albemarle County) goes to the court that summons names. Read the NOTICE on the back and the charge after DESCRIBE CHARGE on the front, and the Virginia Prepayable Offenses Information Sheet if the officer gave you one. If the charge is not on that sheet, or you got no sheet, call the court for instructions. If you lost the ticket, the statewide Online Case Information System lets you search by name (it cannot take payments).
steps.deadline: Before the court date on the summons
steps.quote: Read the “NOTICE” on the back of your summons and the description of your alleged violation, which follows “DESCRIBE CHARGE” on the front of your summons.

steps.step: Check that the offence can be prepaid
steps.how: Only offences on the Supreme Court's Uniform Fine Schedule (Rule 3B:2), or a parallel city ordinance, can be prepaid, plus any city traffic ordinance on a schedule entered by the circuit court (Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(D); no such schedule was found). For other traffic offences Rule 3B:2 says a court hearing is required. State law bars prepaying indictable offences, reckless driving, driving under the influence, leaving the scene of an accident, driving while suspended or revoked, and driving without a licence. Speeding 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph, is reckless driving (Va. Code § 46.2-862), so it cannot be prepaid; the court's speeding table stops at 19 mph over. The court's own sheet lists reckless driving, selling alcohol to a person under 21, over-licence weight and fireworks as not prepayable.
steps.quote: For traffic offenses not listed below, a court hearing is required.

steps.step: Decide whether to prepay or go to court
steps.how: Prepaying is a written guilty plea: you give up the trial, your signed plea has the force of a court judgment, and the conviction is reported to DMV, which may assess demerit points on your licence. To contest the charge, do not prepay; go to court on the date on the summons (step s9).
steps.quote: Pre-court payments are deemed a waiver of a court hearing and entry of a guilty plea.

steps.step: Work out the amount to prepay
steps.how: Use the court's Traffic and Criminal Prepayment Fees sheet (updated 3/21/2025). The total is the fine plus $74.00 costs for a traffic infraction, or $99.00 for a prepayable misdemeanor. Speeding is $6 per mph over the limit (for example, 10 mph over: $60.00 fine, $134.00 total); the sheet shows $7 per mph for a school crossing (§ 46.2-873), and Rule 3B:2 sets $200 plus $8 per mph for a residence district (§ 46.2-878.2). A few offences, such as an adult seat belt violation, carry no costs. For state traffic offences and parallel city ordinances the fines come from the Supreme Court's statewide schedule, so a clerk cannot charge a different fine. The sheet also lists some city ordinance and non-traffic offences (for example the taxi, dog and noise ordinances).
steps.fee: The fine on the schedule plus $74.00 costs for a traffic infraction (see fees)

steps.who: Person charged, paying the Charlottesville General District Court
steps.how: Open the General District Court Online Case Information System and choose the court named at the top of the summons (Charlottesville General District Court). Search by name, case number or hearing date. If the case shows Mark For Payment, mark it (up to five cases on one receipt), choose Process Payment, pay by credit or debit card, and print the confirmation screen as your receipt. Payments made after 3:30 pm are processed the next business day.
steps.deadline: Before 3:30 pm on the business day before the trial date
steps.fee: Fine and costs, plus a 4% card convenience fee per transaction
steps.quote: Payment must be made prior to 3:30 pm on the business day before the trial date to ensure the payment will be processed before the court date.

steps.how: Follow all the instructions in the PRETRIAL WAIVER AND PREPAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS section of the summons, and mail the payment to the court named on the summons: Charlottesville General District Court, P. O. Box 2677, Charlottesville, VA 22902. District courts accept personal checks, money orders, certified checks and credit cards; make a check payable to the court (Charlottesville General District Court). For a card, confirm with the court which cards it accepts and fill in the Credit Card Authorization on the back of the prepayable offenses sheet. The state court system advises mailing at least 7 days before the court date. The payment counts only when the court receives it, and a further fee is added if it arrives after the court date. Do not mail it to the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court.
steps.deadline: It must reach the court before the court date; the state court system advises mailing it at least 7 days before
steps.quote: Prepayment of the fine(s) and fee(s) is effective only upon receipt by the applicable general district court, not on the date that you mail it.

steps.step: Or prepay in person at the Clerk's Office
steps.who: Person charged, at the General District Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Go to the Clerk's Office at 606 E Market Street, Charlottesville, Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. District courts must accept personal checks and credit or debit cards; the city's Traffic & Criminal Fees page also lists cash, and a 4% fee for cards (Visa, MasterCard or Discover). The office processes no payments after 4:15 pm. A drop box next to the Clerk's Office door takes after-hours drop-offs.
steps.deadline: Before the court date; no payments are processed after 4:15 pm
steps.fee: Fine and costs; 4% convenience fee for a credit or debit card
steps.quote: This office cannot process any payments after 4:15 pm.

steps.step: If you need a new court date, ask for a continuance
steps.who: Person charged, to the Clerk's Office (or the Commonwealth's Attorney); a judge decides later requests
steps.how: In traffic cases the Clerk or the Commonwealth's Attorney can grant a first continuance of no more than 30 days. The court's state page says the clerk's office may give a prepayable offence one continuance, to the officer's next court date. A second continuance needs a motion to the judge. For a traffic misdemeanor (such as reckless driving), the court's state page says to contact the Commonwealth's Attorney's office for a continuance date and submit the agreed date to the judge in writing before the court date. Once a continuance is granted, Form DC-344 lets you promise in writing to appear on the new date, so the court shall not require you to appear on the original date; you sign it before a judge, clerk, deputy clerk or notary and certify that you gave a copy to the attorney for the Commonwealth. The court may still require you to appear on the original date if you are in violation of the terms of your pretrial release or have failed to appear before.
steps.quote: The clerk's office may grant a one-time continuance of prepayable offenses to the involved officer's next court date.

steps.step: To contest the ticket, go to trial on the court date
steps.who: Person charged; a General District Court judge decides
steps.how: Appear at the Charlottesville General District Court, 606 E Market Street, at the date and time on the summons. Traffic infractions and prepayable cases are heard on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, in slots set by the officer's court schedule. A judge decides a traffic infraction without a jury, and you are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. You can plead guilty, not guilty or nolo contendere, hire a lawyer, and ask the clerk's office to subpoena witnesses (Form DC-325, which asks for requests at least ten days before the trial). The prepayment schedule does not limit the fine the judge can set.
steps.deadline: The court date on the summons
steps.fee: If found guilty: the fine the judge sets plus costs, including the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction
steps.quote: You have the right to have the clerk's office subpoena witnesses to appear in court on your behalf.

steps.step: Know what happens if you neither prepay nor appear
steps.how: If you neither prepay nor appear for a traffic infraction, you are deemed to have waived a hearing: the case can be tried without you, the court notifies you of its finding, and a $35 failure-to-appear cost is added unless you ask for a hearing and show good cause. For a traffic infraction the court does not issue a failure-to-appear warrant under Va. Code § 46.2-938. In criminal and certain traffic cases (traffic misdemeanors) a separate failure-to-appear charge may be brought.
steps.fee: $35 added to costs after a trial in absence
steps.quote: In criminal and certain traffic cases, if you fail to pre-pay the fine and costs (when allowed) and also fail to appear in court, a separate warrant may be issued against you on a new charge of failure to appear.

steps.step: After a conviction, pay or get time to pay
steps.who: Person convicted, at the General District Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: The clerk tells you the total (the judge's fine plus processing fees). Pay that day at the Clerk's Office (cash, check or credit card; 4% card fee), or ask for time. If you need time to pay and did not ask for it in court (or did not appear), you must go to the Clerk's Office. For time to pay you sign a DC-210 Fines and Costs Payment Agreement with a 30- or 90-day due date and pay monthly; a 90-day deferred plan has a one-time $10 fee, and by statute the court may not require a down payment on a first plan (see caveats on the city's extension rule). If your sole financial resource is a Social Security benefit or Supplemental Security Income, tell the clerk: state law exempts you from making payments, and the case is not sent to collections. You can ask at the clerk's office for community service credit (no record of violent offences, and the service site must approve you); you get 90 days to do the hours, credited at the higher of the federal or Virginia minimum wage. You can also petition in writing on Form DC-211.
steps.deadline: The 30- or 90-day due date on the DC-210; a payment within 10 days of a due date counts as on time
steps.fee: $10 one-time fee for a 90-day deferred payment plan
steps.quote: You will be asked to sign a DC-210 Fines and Costs Payment Agreement.

steps.step: Pay later online or by mail, before the account goes to collection
steps.how: Online, in the same General District Court system, from 6:00 am the day after the trial (not on the trial date). By mail, call the court for the amount and your reference case number, write the number on your check, and mail it to the court where the case was heard. Without a payment agreement, an unpaid balance goes to collection 90 days after the court date, and interest accrues from 181 days after it. The city's page warns of a 17% Commonwealth fee and possible garnishment.
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the court date, unless you have a payment agreement
steps.fee: Up to a 17% collection fee, plus interest, if unpaid (see fees)
steps.quote: If you have not entered into a “time to pay” or deferred payment agreement and the court has not received your payment within 90 days following your court date, your account will be sent to collection.

steps.step: Appeal a conviction to the Circuit Court
steps.who: Person convicted, by notice to the General District Court clerk; the Charlottesville Circuit Court hears the appeal
steps.how: File a notice of appeal with the Charlottesville General District Court clerk within ten days of the conviction, whatever your plea. The Circuit Court (315 East High Street) tries the case again from the start, and for a traffic infraction you have the right to a jury; ask the Circuit Court clerk about scheduling a jury trial. The city's Circuit Court page says criminal and traffic appeal cases are set at 9:30 am at term (terms begin the third Monday of April, June, August, October and December, and the Tuesday after the third Monday in February). No new bond is required. You can withdraw the appeal before it is heard, by written notice to the court and the prosecutor before the hearing date, and pay the fine and costs; a withdrawal within ten days of the conviction adds no costs, while a later one leads the Circuit Court to affirm the judgment and tax costs.
steps.deadline: Within ten days of the conviction
steps.quote: If you wish to appeal your case to the circuit court, you must file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the general district court within ten days of the judgment or conviction by the general district court.

caveats: The City Code has not been checked. The city publishes its Code of Ordinances on Municode (https://library.municode.com/va/charlottesville/codes/code_of_ordinances); Municode's terms of use page answered HTTP 520 on 2026-10-10, so Municode text is treated as not reusable. City traffic ordinances that parallel state law are prepayable under Rule 3B:2; no circuit court schedule for non-parallel city ordinances (Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(D)) was found. The court's prepayment sheet lists a few City Code sections (for example 15-246 bike or moped riding on the Mall, 15-242 moped helmet, 16-9 amplified noise from a vehicle), cited here only as the sheet shows them.
The two local legal_basis entries are court policies posted on the city's court pages, not City Code sections.

Conflict: the city's Parking Tickets page (https://www.charlottesville.gov/557/Parking-Tickets) says the Treasurer's Office does not accept moving violations and that they must be paid at the Police Department. No court page says this; the court pages and Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(B) send prepayments to the General District Court clerk (or a magistrate). Pay the court named on the summons.

The $74.00 infraction cost on the court's sheet is not broken down. By law it includes the $51 fixed fee, which applies to a written appearance with a guilty plea (Va. Code § 16.1-69.48:1(A)(ii) and (D), shown as Code 460 on the sheet). The sheet also lists Code 121 (TIA) $35.00, which matches the $35 trial-in-absence cost, and Code 244 (CHSF) $20.00, Code 137 (TTP) $10.00 and Code 001 (I.C.C.F.) $15.00 without saying when they apply. Va. Code § 53.1-120(D) allows a local courthouse security assessment of up to $20, but the sheet does not expand CHSF, so the link is not confirmed. The sheet is dated 3/21/2025 and may not reflect later changes.

The speeding rows on the court's sheet are labelled confusingly. Its header reads '46.2-873 $7/mph', and the note '46.2-878 safety zone add fee of $200' sits next to '$8.00 per mile over the speed limit'. Rule 3B:2 sets $200 plus $8 per mph for speeding in a residence district (Va. Code § 46.2-878.2), and Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(A) fixes the § 46.2-878.2 prepayable fine at $200 plus a per-mph amount. Check the sheet against the summons, or call the court.
Quotes from the court's prepayment sheet are table rows (for example '35/25 - 45/35 10 60.00 134.00' is the row for 10 mph over: fine, then total). They are matched to the PDF's text.

The court's payment policy PDF on vacourts.gov (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/online/ppp_fines_costs/dc/charlottesville.pdf) is a scanned image with no text layer, so no quote is taken from it; the Traffic Division phone number comes from its letterhead. It calls the DC-210 an 'Acknowledgement of Suspension or Revocation of Driver's license', while the city's Traffic & Criminal Fees page calls it a 'Fines and Costs Payment Agreement'. The DC-210 is not on the vacourts.gov list of district court forms people fill in themselves; the city's page says you will be asked to sign it at the Clerk's Office, so it is not listed as a form here.

Continuance rules are worded differently. The city's court page says the Clerk or the Commonwealth's Attorney may grant a first traffic continuance of up to 30 days. The court's vacourts.gov page says the clerk's office may grant a prepayable offence one continuance, to the officer's next court date, and that misdemeanours can only be continued through the Commonwealth's Attorney's office. The Commonwealth's Attorney's own channels are not covered here.

Card brands differ by channel. The city's Payments page says online card payments are Visa or MasterCard (4% fee); the Clerk's Office takes Visa, MasterCard or Discover (4% fee). The vacourts.gov page tells mail payers to confirm with the court which cards it accepts.

Prepaying is a conviction on a guilty plea. Va. Code § 16.1-132 allows an appeal within ten days 'whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty', but no Charlottesville page says how the ten days are counted after a mailed or online prepayment, or what the conviction date is.

No official Charlottesville page says whether the General District Court accepts a driver improvement clinic, community service or other terms in exchange for reducing or dismissing a traffic charge. Va. Code § 46.2-505 lets a court require a clinic, and § 46.2-498 covers voluntary clinics for DMV safe driving points. Ask the court or a lawyer.
DMV demerit points, insurance effects and license suspension rules are not covered here beyond the court pamphlet's statement that DMV assesses points for certain convictions.

Form DC-324 (Notice, Appearance, Waiver and Plea, https://www.vacourts.gov/static/forms/district/dc324.pdf) exists but cites Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:2, the statute for non-traffic offences, so it is not listed as a traffic form. A traffic summons carries its own PRETRIAL WAIVER AND PREPAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS section.

The 17% Commonwealth fee is stated on the city's court pages, but no section of the Code of Virginia cited here sets that rate. Va. Code § 19.2-349 lets collection start 90 days after judgment and pays private collectors on a contingency basis.

The index versions of Va. Code § 19.2-354 and § 19.2-349 are marked effective until January 1, 2027. Their replacement text was not in the index, so the plan-fee, community service and collection rules may change on that date.

The vacourts.gov court page lists a phone number under the Clerk of Court's name, and the city page shows the same number next to the clerk's name. It was left out as a possible individual line; the general Clerk's Office line and the Traffic Division line are given instead. No staff or judges are named here. The Circuit Court's installment guidelines and community service order (city DocumentCenter files 2081 and 16459) are Circuit Court documents that name staff, so they are not used for the General District Court steps.
The online payment system (eapps.courts.state.va.us) refuses automated readers, so it is not described here; the online steps come from the vacourts.gov instructions page.

Circuit Court appeal costs, the circuit court payment rules after an appeal, and the deadline and procedure for an appeal to the Court of Appeals of Virginia (Rules of Court, Part 5A) are not covered here. A General District Court conviction is reported to DMV only after the appeal period passes with no appeal perfected (Va. Code § 46.2-383(A)).
Commercial driver's license holders face different rules (for example, Va. Code § 46.2-505(B) bars reducing or dismissing their charges for clinic attendance). They are not covered here.

Possible conflict: Va. Code § 19.2-354.1(E) says no court shall require a down payment on a first deferred, modified deferred or installment agreement (only on a subsequent agreement). The city's Traffic & Criminal Fees page says that when you extend a due date, 'you will make a payment towards the amount due at this time'; the court's scanned policy (an image with no text layer) appears to limit this to when a payment was not recently made. Neither page says whether that payment is required or what happens without it. Ask the clerk, and cite § 19.2-354.1(E) if a down payment is demanded on a first agreement.
The 4% card fee is stated for online payments (vacourts.gov) and at the Clerk's Office (the city's pages). No page says whether the fee applies to a card authorization mailed with a prepayment.

Circuit Court appeal scheduling is worded differently. The city's Circuit Court page says criminal and traffic appeal cases are set at 9:30 am at term; the court's vacourts.gov page names only misdemeanor appeal cases at 9:30 am. Neither gives the exact day, so check the notice or ask the Circuit Court clerk.

corrections: All 70 original quotes confirmed: 41 state-law quotes are substrings (whitespace normalised only) of I.text_of for the cited section; 29 local and procedure quotes were found word for word in the official pages and PDFs re-fetched on 2026-10-11 (city court pages, the city's prepayment fee PDF, vacourts.gov court page, ticket instructions, GDC pamphlet and Rule 3B:2 in the Rules of Court PDF). The fee-sheet rows match the PDF text in content order and the rendered table; the layout-mode extraction misaligns the middle column (for example it pairs 125.00 199.00 with the moped helmet row), so it was not used.

Seven state-law quotes added, each checked against I.text_of: § 46.2-862 (speeding 20 mph over or above 85 mph is reckless driving), § 19.2-258.1 (judge-only trial of infractions in district court; trial in absence with notice and no § 46.2-938 warrant; jury right on appeal), § 19.2-354.1(J) (no referral to collections for Social Security or SSI), § 19.2-266.3 (exception to the waiver of appearance) and § 16.1-133 (written notice to withdraw an appeal).

s13: the draft said appeals are set at 9:30 am 'on the first day of the court's term'. The city's Circuit Court page says criminal and traffic appeal cases are 'set at 9:30 am at term'; only grand juries are on the first day. Fixed, with the term dates from that page.

s11: the draft said 'If your only income is Social Security or SSI'. The statute and the city page say 'sole financial resource', which is broader than income. Fixed, and added that such a case is not sent to collections (§ 19.2-354.1(J)).

s2: the draft said only Rule 3B:2 offences or parallel city ordinances can be prepaid. § 16.1-69.40:1(D) also allows non-parallel city traffic ordinances on a circuit court schedule (none found), and § 16.1-69.40:1(A) also bars indictable offences. Added both, and that speeding 20 mph or more over, or over 85 mph, is reckless driving and cannot be prepaid.

s4: 'The fines come from the Supreme Court's statewide schedule' was too broad; the sheet also lists city ordinance and non-traffic offences (taxi, dog, noise). Scoped to state offences and parallel ordinances, and added the $7 school-crossing and residence-district ($200 plus $8 per mph) rates.

s6: mailing at least 7 days before the court date is advice on vacourts.gov ('should be mailed'), not a rule; the deadline now says the payment must reach the court before the court date and gives the 7 days as advice. Added: make the check payable to the court, and confirm which cards it accepts.
Card-fee item said '(online, by mail or in person)'. The 4% fee is stated only for online payments and at the Clerk's Office; by mail is not stated. Item fixed and a caveat added.

'May' kept: the returned-check fee (§ 19.2-353.3, 'may impose') and the $10 plan fee (§ 19.2-354(A), 'may assess a one-time fee not to exceed $10') now say so in the fee amounts. The '46.2-878 safety zone' fee amount was garbled ('$200 added, at $8.00 per mph') and now quotes the sheet's two labels and gives the Rule 3B:2 rate.

s8: added from Form DC-344 that the defendant signs before a judge, clerk, deputy clerk or notary and certifies a copy went to the attorney for the Commonwealth; the § 19.2-266.3 exception (pretrial-release violation or an earlier failure to appear); and the vacourts.gov route for continuing a traffic misdemeanor through the Commonwealth's Attorney's office.

s9: added that a judge decides a traffic infraction without a jury and the presumption of innocence (§ 19.2-258.1), and Form DC-325 (Request for Witness Subpoena, new form f4), which asks for requests at least ten days before trial.

s10: added from § 19.2-258.1 that a person who neither prepays nor appears for an infraction is deemed to have waived a hearing, is notified of the finding, and is not subject to a § 46.2-938 failure-to-appear warrant; the pamphlet's separate FTA charge is limited to criminal and certain traffic cases.

s11: added that a person who did not ask for time in court must go to the Clerk's Office, the community service terms (90 days; credit at the higher of the federal or Virginia minimum wage), and a pointer to the new down-payment caveat.

s13: added the § 19.2-258.1 jury right for an infraction appeal, the § 16.1-133 written notice to withdraw an appeal, and that a withdrawal more than ten days after conviction leads the Circuit Court to affirm and tax costs.

s1: 'A ticket written in the city goes to the Charlottesville General District Court' softened to 'normally returnable', with the rule to use the court named on the summons. s7: cash is listed on the city's Traffic & Criminal Fees page, now named.

Caveats: the $74 caveat now gives the legal basis for including the $51 fee (§ 16.1-69.48:1(A)(ii) and (D)) and notes Code 121 (TIA) $35.00, matching the $35 trial-in-absence cost; the DC-210 caveat no longer says 'the clerk completes it in the office' (no page says so). New caveats: the down-payment conflict between § 19.2-354.1(E) and the city's extension rule, the card fee by mail, and the Circuit Court appeal scheduling wording.

Local legal_basis citation reworded: the $10 plan fee is a court policy posted on the city's pages, with the fee authorized by § 19.2-354(A) (the draft said 'posted under § 19.2-354(A)'). Summary updated (reckless-driving speeds, judge-only trial, jury on appeal). Sources added: Form DC-325 and §§ 19.2-258.1 and 46.2-862.

Privacy confirmed: no staff, judge or clerk names; the clerk's listed line (shown next to the clerk's name on both court pages) and the Circuit Court clerk's email are not used. Contacts are the Clerk's Office general line, the Traffic Division line (confirmed on the letterhead of the court's scanned payment policy), office addresses, portals and pages.
